findings.message:
The `do_schedule` function is vulnerable to race conditions. Consider the following concurrent execution sequences.

```
Thread A                        |   Thread B
is_scheduled.load() == false    |
                                |   is_scheduled.load() == false
is_scheduled.store(true)        |
push_front(taskless.clone()     |
                                |   is_scheduled.store(true)
                                |   push_front(taskless.clone()
```

Given that fact that this simple `do_schedule` function is vulnerable to race conditions, I am worried about the correctness of `taskless_softirq_handler` under concurrency.

Please examine `taskless_softirq_handler` and `do_schedule` more carefully for potential race conditions. I encourage you to explicitly write out the invariants that must be held despite of concurrency. These invariants will be very helpful to reason about the correctness of the code.
findings.tp_fp_justification: New do_schedule uses check-then-act (is_scheduled.load then store) instead of an atomic RMW; tatetian gives a concrete two-thread interleaving where the same taskless is pushed twice, breaking the documented no-concurrent-execution invariant. Introduced by this PR (new file); author later fixed with compare_exchange.
